name: snatching by the sídhe

attributes.attribute: the fairy folk who took humans
a fairy or a stone left in place of the taken one

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Snatching by the sídhe is the fairy stealing of people. The fairies often took from the world of the humans. The sweetest things and the best people were at the most risk. Families used small charms to guard against the threat. A secret or a strange name was kept around a child. Mothers kept the trousers of a husband in the bed to drive the fairies away. The folk might take a bride before the wedding, or carry a child and leave a changeling in the cradle. A stone could be left in the place of the taken one. The whole family stood in danger, and a nurse, a child, or the beautiful could be carried off at once. The taking is a central fear in the lore of the sídhe and of the changeling.
